learningModules.title: Module 1: The Pre-Value Integration Gate — What It Is and How to Confirm It's Yours
learningModules.description: The activation-killing pattern you described in your intake, and the specific analytics you'd need to instrument to confirm it's actually happening in your funnel.
learningModules.content:
You told us onboarding drops off around the analytics-integration step. We can't confirm the exact shape of that drop-off — your onboarding runs inside your authenticated product, and we only have access to what's publicly reachable (your signup page scored 61/100 on mobile PageSpeed, for context, but that's a different page than the one you're describing).

The pattern you're describing — a step that requires leaving the product, finding credentials, and returning before any value is shown — is a well-documented SaaS activation killer. Users at that point haven't yet experienced the aha-moment that would justify the effort, so the cognitive cost of integration exceeds their motivation by default.

How to confirm this is actually your problem: instrument `onboarding_step_complete` (with a step number) and `first_insight_viewed` in PostHog or your analytics tool of choice. Run it for a week before changing anything. If step 3 shows a sharp completion drop relative to steps 1–2, and churn is concentrated among users who never reach `first_insight_viewed`, that's your own measured confirmation — not a pattern applied to your funnel, but your actual behavior.

Until you have that data, treat every percentage in this document as an illustration of the pattern, not a fact about Growthly.

learningModules.title: Module 2: Demo Data Bypass — The Aha-Moment First Fix
learningModules.description: Implement a sample data bypass that lets users experience the core product value before requiring any integration effort — the fix we'd recommend testing first.
learningModules.content:
The fix has two components: a bypass option and a re-engagement trigger.

Component 1 — Demo Data Bypass: Add a secondary CTA below the integration form. Label: 'Explore with benchmark data →'. This routes users into a fully functional dashboard seeded with anonymized benchmark data from your industry vertical. The data should be realistic and slightly better than average — aspirational but credible.

Design note: the bypass button must not look like an escape hatch. It should look like the smarter path. Use the same visual weight as the primary integration CTA. Never label it 'Skip' — frame it as acceleration, not avoidance.

Component 2 — Re-engagement trigger: On day 2 (after users have interacted with demo data 2+ times), trigger an in-app message: 'You've explored [X] reports in demo mode. Connect your real data to see your actual numbers — it takes 90 seconds.' Now the integration request arrives post-value, not pre-value.

We can't give you a specific expected activation number without your baseline — that's what Module 1's instrumentation is for. What published research on this pattern supports is directional: value-before-commitment onboarding sequences outperform integration-gated ones.

learningModules.title: Module 3: Activation Telemetry — The Events That Would Actually Tell You Something
learningModules.description: Instrument your onboarding sequence with PostHog events to measure activation health and confirm (or disprove) this diagnosis with your own data.
learningModules.content:
Deploy in this exact priority order:

1. posthog.capture('onboarding_step_complete', { step: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 }) — your funnel spine
2. posthog.capture('integration_attempted') — distinguishes intent from completion
3. posthog.capture('integration_completed') — the hard gate metric
4. posthog.capture('demo_data_activated') — measures bypass adoption, once shipped
5. posthog.capture('first_insight_viewed') — the aha-moment indicator
6. posthog.capture('re_engagement_prompt_clicked') — measures day-2 trigger effectiveness, once shipped

Build two PostHog funnels once you have data: the current path (step_1 → step_2 → integration_attempted → integration_completed → first_insight_viewed) and, after shipping the bypass, the new path (step_1 → step_2 → demo_data_activated → first_insight_viewed → integration_completed). Comparing these — with your own numbers — is what would actually confirm or refute this diagnosis.

learningModules.title: Module 4: Weekly Activation Review Ritual
learningModules.description: The 15-minute weekly process to monitor activation health and iterate systematically once you have real data flowing.
learningModules.content:
Every Monday, 15 minutes, in this order, once instrumentation from Module 3 is live:

1. Open your PostHog funnel dashboard. Check the step_1 → first_insight_viewed conversion rate. If it moved more than ±5 points from the prior week, investigate the cause before making any changes.

2. Review demo_data_activated / total_signups ratio, once the bypass is shipped. If it's low, the bypass button may not be prominent enough.

3. Check re_engagement_prompt_clicked rate (day-2 trigger). If it's low, the message copy or timing likely needs adjustment.

4. Review integration_completed rate among users who initially took the demo path — this is your proxy for whether the deferred-gate strategy is actually converting people, not just delaying the same drop-off.

Rule: change one variable per week maximum. Testing two changes simultaneously makes it impossible to attribute any performance delta to a specific cause.

diagnosis.signal: You described onboarding drop-off concentrated at the analytics-integration step in your intake. We have not measured your actual step-by-step funnel — Growthly's onboarding runs inside your authenticated product, which sits outside what a public scan can reach. What we can say is that a step requiring users to leave the product, retrieve credentials, and return before seeing any value is a well-documented activation-killer in SaaS onboarding research. Whether that's costing you what it typically costs comparable products depends on data only you have.

friction.mechanism: Context-Switch Cascade — Pre-Value Integration Gate (modeled from your intake description)
friction.rootCause: A step requiring several sequential actions across two platforms before any product value is shown is a documented churn point — the cognitive cost of the integration exceeds motivation before trust has been established. We can't confirm this is your specific failure point without your own funnel data; the fix below is cheap and reversible enough to be worth testing regardless.

finalDecision.label: Add a demo-data bypass at the integration step
finalDecision.action: Add a secondary CTA below the integration form: 'Explore with benchmark data →', routing users into a fully functional demo environment seeded with anonymized industry benchmark data. Deploy the day-2 re-engagement trigger to convert demo users to real integrations. Instrument the funnel events in Module 3 before shipping, so you have a before/after measurement.
finalDecision.reasoning: Of the three approaches, this is the lowest-risk test of the pattern we modeled — it doesn't remove the integration option, it defers it past a value moment, and you can measure the effect directly against your own baseline within a few weeks.
finalDecision.tradeoff: Requires building a seeded demo state with realistic data — generic placeholder data will undercut the effect. And this entire plan is only as good as the instrumentation in Module 1; skip that and you'll ship a change you can't actually evaluate.

decisions.label: Add demo data bypass at the integration step
decisions.action: Add a secondary CTA below the integration form: 'Explore with benchmark data →'. This routes users into a fully functional demo environment seeded with anonymized industry benchmark data. Deploy the day-2 re-engagement trigger to convert demo users to real integrations.
decisions.reasoning: Removes the hard gate without eliminating the integration option. Published activation research associates value-before-commitment sequencing with meaningfully higher return-to-integrate rates than forced-cold integration — but that's a benchmark, not a measurement of Growthly specifically. Engineering estimate: 3–5 days.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires building a seeded demo state. Data quality and realism matter — generic placeholder data reduces the aha-moment impact.

decisions.label: Remove the integration gate from onboarding entirely — defer to day 3
decisions.action: Eliminate the integration step from onboarding entirely. Grant immediate dashboard access with demo data on sign-up. Trigger the integration prompt on day 3 via in-app message after users have viewed 2+ insights.
decisions.reasoning: Value precedes commitment more completely than option A. If your dashboard functions meaningfully with demo data alone, this is the stronger structural fix — but it's a bigger product change with more surface area to get wrong.
decisions.tradeoff: The dashboard must function meaningfully with demo data alone. If your core value proposition requires live data to be non-trivially better than the demo, this approach needs a high-quality demo layer, not a placeholder.

decisions.label: Replace API key entry with one-click OAuth for the top platforms
decisions.action: Replace the API key form with OAuth buttons for the analytics platforms your users are most likely already on. Auto-detect the most common configuration. Reduce the multi-step context switch to a single authorized click.
decisions.reasoning: OAuth eliminates the credential-hunting friction entirely and is a trusted, recognized pattern. We don't know which platforms your users are actually on — you'd need to check your own signup data before prioritizing which OAuth integration to build first.
decisions.tradeoff: OAuth implementation requires engineering work per platform. Start with the single highest-frequency platform once you know what that is.
